name: sol_mccc_6
description: Hardcoded ERC20 decimal assumptions causing cross-chain accounting errors
question: The source file in `source` handles token amounts transferred or bridged between chains but hardcodes a fixed decimals value (e.g., 18) or omits calling the token's decimals() function when scaling/converting amounts, instead of dynamically reading and normalizing decimals per chain/token, causing incorrect amount calculations when the same token has different decimals on different chains, excluding single-chain-only logic or code that already calls decimals() or applies chain-specific decimal adjustment.
criteria: Scales a bridged amount by a hardcoded 10**18 factor instead of querying the token's decimals()
Mints or credits a wrapped token assuming the source token always has 18 decimals regardless of actual chain-specific decimals
Decodes a cross-chain message amount and applies a constant decimal conversion constant without checking the destination token's decimals
Compares or sums token balances from different chains without normalizing for differing decimals values
